preamble: The shift from the open central vowel [a] to the open-mid back unrounded vowel [ʌ] (the caret) is a backing and raising of the low vowel. In the Godié branch of Eastern Kru, Proto-Eastern Kru *a gave a new central-back vowel ʌ in many words (*ka³ 'have' > kʌ³), while peripheral /a/ was also kept. In St Petersburg Russian, unstressed /a/ (including /a/ from /o/) after a hard consonant in the syllable before the stress, and word-initially, is [ʌ]: сады [sʌˈd̪ˠɨⁱ] 'gardens', where Moscow pronunciation has [ɐ].

examples.note: Superscript digits are Marchese Zogbo's tone levels; the reconstruction rests on Dida, Neyo, Guibéroua and Daloa Bété forms.
Marchese Zogbo finds few conditioning factors; Godié keeps peripheral /a/ alongside the new central vowel /ʌ/.
